Add tomatoes, potato cubes, and the Royco/Pilau spice, then cook until soft.
Add the washed rice and stir for 1 minute until it absorbs the oil.
Pour in water (double the amount of rice), bring to boil, cover tightly, and simmer on low heat.

Place the stuffed smokie on the chapati, roll it up tightly, and wrap it in a nylon bag.

fields.name: Matoke
fields.description: A traditional, heavy green banana dish made affordable for student budgets by omitting meat.
fields.steps:
Coat your hands with oil to prevent sticky sap, then peel the green bananas and potatoes.
Fry onions in a sufuria until soft, then add tomatoes and cook until they turn into a thick paste.
Add the peeled bananas and potato cubes, stirring well to coat them in the tomato mixture.
Dissolve the Royco cube in 2 cups of water, pour into the sufuria, cover, and boil on medium heat for 20 minutes until soft.

fields.cooking_tip: If the bananas are too tough, soak them in hot water for 5 minutes before peeling.

fields.steps:
Cook a firm block of ugali in the first sufuria using water and flour, then set aside.
In the second sufuria, fry onions heavily, then add tomatoes and mash them thoroughly.
Mix the Royco powder in half a cup of cold water and pour it over the tomatoes.
Simmer for 3 minutes to create a thick, salty red gravy to pour over your ugali chunks.
